# Adjudication Task — Chapter 376

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃376화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|인산인해(人山人海).
  6|
  7|그렇게밖에 표현할 수 없는 광경이었다.
  8|
  9|산서잠룡, 아니 열화신룡 진태경과 화산신룡 청풍이 떠난다는 소식을 들은 사람들이 구름처럼 모여들었기 때문이었다.
 10|
 11|비단 무림인뿐만 아니라 겁 없는 양민들까지 더해지니, 배웅에 나선 인파는 꼬리에 꼬리를 물고 늘어져 셀 수가 없었다.
 12|
 13|“잘 가시오! 열화신룡!”
 14|
 15|“사천 무림은 그대들을 잊지 않을 거요!”
 16|
 17|“뿔 달린 뱀이다! 화산신룡이 뿔 달린 뱀을 갖고 있다!”
 18|
 19|“헉, 뱀이 공중제비를 돌았다!”
 20|
 21|“화왕! 화왕이 뱀을 붙잡아서 태우려고 하고 있다!”
 22|
 23|웅성거리는 소음이 행렬을 따라 서서히 멀어져 간다.
 24|
 25|그리고 아무도 찾지 않는 언덕 위, 나무 그루터기에 앉아 모든 광경을 지켜보고 있던 소년이 문득 입을 열었다.
 26|
 27|“멀리도 왔구나.”
 28|
 29|“그러게 말입니다. 힘이 드는군요.”
 30|
 31|거친 숨소리와 함께 풀밭에 털썩 주저앉는 늙은 제자의 모습에 소년, 문경은 중얼거렸다.
 32|
 33|“……참으로 멀리도 왔어.”
 34|
 35|거리를 말하는 것이 아니다. 지금 문경은 지나온 세월을 이야기하고 있었다.
 36|
 37|“우리가 처음 만났던 때를 기억하느냐?”
 38|
 39|“어찌 잊을 수 있겠습니까.”
 40|
 41|늙은 제자는 이마에 맺힌 땀을 훔쳤다. 마치 그날의 따가운 햇볕이 자신에게 내리쬐고 있는 것처럼.
 42|
 43|“홍무(洪武) 일 년. 유난히도 무더웠던 그해 여름을.”
 44|
 45|황위를 둘러싼 내전이 끝나고 새로운 천자가 즉위한 해였다.
 46|
 47|젊고 야심만만한 황제는 연호(年號)를 바꾸고 개혁을 꾀했으나, 기나긴 내전으로 피폐해진 백성들은 천자의 뜻을 받들어 개혁에 동참하기에는 너무나 지쳐 있었다.
 48|
 49|“천하 각지에서 반란이 일어나고, 도적이 들끓었지.”
 50|
 51|“가뭄이 들고 메뚜기 떼가 평야를 휩쓸었습니다. 관군과 반란군의 시신이 도처에 가득하니 역병이 창궐했지요.”
 52|
 53|“그래, 실로 난세(亂世)였다.”
 54|
 55|죽음은 또 다른 죽음을 낳았고 이내 대륙을 집어삼켰다.
 56|
 57|동씨 성을 쓰는 젊은 목수 역시 천하에 드리워진 어두운 그림자를 피할 수는 없었다.
 58|
 59|“지금도 가끔 그때를 생각하고는 합니다.”
 60|
 61|수십 년의 세월이 바꿔 놓은 것은 강산뿐만이 아니다. 사랑하는 두 아이와 아내를 역병으로 잃어야 했던 젊은 목수는 어느덧 늙은 의원이 되어 있었다.
 62|
 63|“제가 조금만 빨랐더라면, 더 빨리 스승님을 찾았다면 가족들을 살릴 수 있지 않았을까 하는 생각 말입니다.”
 64|
 65|“후회하느냐?”
 66|
 67|“예.”
 68|
 69|하늘과 가까운 언덕에 앉아, 떠다니는 조각구름을 바라보는 늙은 의원의 눈동자는 어느새 젊은 목수의 그것으로 돌아가 있었다.
 70|
 71|“이 숨이 붙어 있는 한 평생토록.”
 72|
 73|고작 하루 차이였다.
 74|
 75|목수가 역병에 걸린 몸을 이끌고 화전민촌에 머무르던 이름 모를 노의원을 데려왔을 때는 모든 것이 늦은 후였다.
 76|
 77|그는 꼬박 하루를 울었고 가족들을 묻기 위한 구덩이를 팠다. 그리고 자신이 데려온 의원에게 한 가지 부탁을 했다.
 78|
 79|“함께 묻어 주십시오. 제가 그리 청했지요.”
 80|
 81|문경이 무뚝뚝한 목소리로 말을 받았다.
 82|
 83|“그래서 나는 네 뺨을 때려 주었지.”
 84|
 85|“많이 아팠습니다. 죽고 싶을 정도로.”
 86|
 87|아팠다. 목숨을 좌지우지하는 고통보다는 사랑하는 아내와 아이들을 더 이상 볼 수 없다는 사실 때문에.
 88|
 89|“그런 저를 스승님께서 일으켜 세워 주셨습니다.”
 90|
 91|문경은 고개를 저었다.
 92|
 93|“손을 내밀었을 뿐이다. 그 손을 붙잡고 일어난 것은 네 의지였어.”
 94|
 95|“살아야 했습니다. 해야 할 일이 생겼으니까요.”
 96|
 97|본래대로라면 목수 역시 역병으로 죽었어야 할 몸이었다.
 98|
 99|그러나 의원은 지금껏 본 적 없는 의술로 그를 완치시켰고, 목수는 처음으로 하늘이 정한 생로병사(生老病死)를 한낱 인간 역시 바꿀 수 있음을 깨달았다.
100|
101|“아직도 눈앞에 선하구나. 제자로 받아 달라며 무릎을 꿇던 네 모습이.”
102|
103|“이 제자가 기억하는 것과는 다르군요. 저는 따라오라며 손짓하시던 스승님의 모습이 떠오릅니다.”
104|
105|그렇게 가족을 잃은 젊은 목수는 새로운 목표를 찾았고, 천하를 주유하며 힘없고 가난한 병자를 보살피던 늙은 의원은 새로운 제자를 얻었다.
106|
107|이제는 의원이 된 목수, 동봉(童奉)이 스승의 진정한 정체를 알게 된 것은 그로부터 오랜 시간이 흐른 뒤였다.
108|
109|“살성(殺星)…… 실로 무시무시한 별호입니다. 그때 처음으로 스승님이 낯설게 느껴졌지요.”
110|
111|문경은 무감각한 시선으로 저 너머를 바라봤다.
112|
113|지금부터 하려는 말은 그가 자신의 제자에게 단 한 번도 묻지 않았던 내용이었다.
114|
115|“왜 떠나지 않았느냐?”
116|
117|“제가 스승님을 떠날 것이라 생각하셨습니까?”
118|
119|“나는 지금까지 헤아릴 수 없이 많은 목숨을 해쳤다. 과거를 숨긴 추악한 살귀(殺鬼)에 불과했지. 네가 떠난다 해도 이해했을 것이다.”
120|
121|“정말 그랬을지도 모르지요. 하지만 저는 스승님이 어떤 사람인지 너무나도 잘 알고 있었습니다.”
122|
123|다음 순간, 나지막한 목소리가 이어졌다.
124|
125|“신의(神醫). 제 스승님은 신의라 불리는 분입니다. 이유 없는 살생을 저지르실 분이 아닙니다.”
126|
127|“……!”
128|
129|문경의 눈동자가 파르르 떨렸다. 그건 지금껏 아무에게도 말하지 않았고, 아무도 인정하지 않으려 했던 사실이었다.
130|
131|그는 살수로 살아오며 정(正), 사(邪), 마(魔)를 가리지 않고 숱한 목숨을 직접 거둬들였다. 그리고 그들은 하나같이 죽어야 할 이유가 있는 자들이었다.
132|
133|공명정대함으로 이름 높은 정파의 대협은 여인을 간살하는 취미가 있었고, 어느 사파의 고수는 재미 삼아 촌락 하나를 몰살시켰다.
134|
135|중원을 침공한 마교의 군세가 닥치는 대로 사람들을 죽이고 파괴를 일삼지 않았다면, 보다 못한 천하제일의 살수가 나서서 악명 높은 마두들을 죽이지 않았다면 그는 살성(殺星)이라 불릴 수 없었을 것이다.
136|
137|“내가 마교와 싸우지 않았다면, 온 천하가 나를 손가락질했을 것이다. 지금껏 그래 왔던 것처럼.”
138|
139|살성이라는 별호는 천하 무림의 주인이 된 정파가 그에게 내리는 면죄부이자 강자에 대한 찬사일 뿐이었다.
140|
141|문경은 늘 문경이었음에도, 사람들은 그 이면에 숨겨진 진실을 알지 못했고 알려고도 하지 않았다.
142|
143|“어째서 알리지 않으셨습니까?”
144|
145|“모두 지난 일이다. 나는 무림을 떠나고자 했고, 뜻한 바에 따라 의원이 되었지. 그리고 앞으로도 그럴 것이다.”
146|
147|문경은 천천히 몸을 일으켰다. 어느새 사천당문을 빠져나간 기나긴 행렬은 저 너머로 사라진 후였다.
148|
149|“이만 내려가자. 우리를 기다리는 병자들이 있다.”
150|
151|건조한 목소리와 함께 걸음을 뗀 그 순간이었다.
152|
153|“곧 거대한 전란(戰亂)이 일어날 것입니다.”
154|
155|문경의 발걸음이 우뚝 멈췄다. 그의 등 뒤로 늙수그레한 제자의 목소리가 이어졌다.
156|
157|“그때와 같은 일이 반복될 것입니다. 수많은 이들이 죽고 다치겠지요. 부모와 자식을 잃은 자들이 넘쳐나고, 비명과 죽음이 끊이지 않을 겁니다.”
158|
159|“……많이 바빠지겠군. 준비를 해 둬야겠어.”
160|
161|“제가 무슨 말을 하려 하는지, 스승님께서는 알고 계시지 않습니까.”
162|
163|“알고 싶지 않다.”
164|
165|“스승님.”
166|
167|“나는 의원이다. 비록 스스로 약속한 바를 깨고 어쩔 수 없이 살생을 저질렀으나, 두 번 다시 그런 실수는 없을 것이다.”
168|
169|문경은 천천히 말을 이었다.
170|
171|“싸우는 것은 저들의 몫이고, 병자를 치료하는 것은 우리의 몫이다. 내 뜻은 이미 무림을 떠난 지 오래다.”
172|
173|“그렇다면 어찌하여 무공을 놓지 않으셨습니까.”
174|
175|“……!”
176|
177|문경은 말문이 막혔다.
178|
179|그건 스스로가 오랫동안 품고 있던 의문이었다. 살생이 싫어 무림을 떠나고자 했다면, 살생을 위한 수단인 무공 역시 전폐해야 맞았다.
180|
181|그러나 오히려 그의 무공은 한층 진일보했다. 무공에 대한 끈과 미련을 놓지 못했다는 증거다.
182|
183|‘그것은 어째서인가.’
184|
185|짧은 상념을 깨트린 것은 늙은 제자의 목소리였다.
186|
187|“스승님께서는 수백, 수천의 병자를 치료하실 수 있으십니다. 동시에 수만의 인명을 구할 수 있는 분이기도 하지요.”
188|
189|“…….”
190|
191|“살성(殺星)이 아닌 신의(神醫)로서 전란을 막아 주십시오. 이 제자는 이곳에서 병자들을 보살피겠습니다.”
192|
193|문경은 문득 고개를 들어 하늘을 바라봤다.
194|
195|맑고 푸르르다. 사천당문이 피로 물들었던 칠 주야 전의 하늘은 먹구름으로 가득했었다.
196|
197|“하늘이 맑구나.”
198|
199|무뚝뚝한 목소리와 함께 멈춰 있던 발걸음이 앞으로 나아갔다.
200|
201|“이만 병자들을 살피러 가 보아야겠다. 천천히 내려오너라.”
202|
203|언덕을 내려가는 그의 등 뒤로 동봉의 목소리가 흩어졌다.
204|
205|“술시(戌時). 성도의 서쪽 항구에서 출발한다고 했습니다.”
206|
207|“부질없는 짓. 내가 있어야 할 곳은 무림이 아니다.”
208|
209|그러나 서서히 멀어지는 스승의 뒷모습을 바라보는 늙은 제자의 입가에는 희미한 웃음이 맺혀 있었다.
210|
211|“부디…… 강녕하십시오.”
212|
213|휘이이잉.
214|
215|어디선가 불어온 바람이 두 사람의 사이를 스쳐 지나갔다.
216|
217|
218|
219|* * *
220|
221|
222|
223|“뭘 그렇게 보고 계세요?”
224|
225|혁무진의 물음에, 항구를 에워싼 인파를 바라보고 있던 나는 고개를 돌렸다.
226|
227|“별거 아니다. 그냥 혹시나 해서.”
228|
229|“그러니까 뭘요?”
230|
231|“이 자식이, 왜 이렇게 꼬치꼬치 캐물어? 그렇다면 그런 줄 알지.”
232|
233|내 대답에 혁무진이 의미심장하게 웃었다.
234|
235|“사실 다 알고 있습니다. 조장님께서 왜 그러시는지.”
236|
237|“……?”
238|
239|순간 멈칫했다. 이 자식이 어떻게 그걸 알지? 나와 신의가 나눈 대화는 청풍도 듣지 못했는데.
240|
241|‘이 녀석 눈치가 이렇게 빨랐나.’
242|
243|의아해하던 그때, 녀석이 작게 속삭였다.
244|
245|“저기 앞줄 우측 네 번째에 서 있는 소저를 보고 계셨던 거 아닙니까?”
246|
247|“…….”
248|
249|“확실히 예쁘긴 하네요. 제법 있는 집 규수 같아 보이는데. 조장님께서 허락하신다면 오른팔인 제가 슬쩍 가서 따로 자리를…….”
250|
251|“무진아.”
252|
253|“예? 아, 혹시 자연스러운 만남을 추구하시는 쪽입니까? 그렇다면…….”
254|
255|“장강 밑바닥에 가라앉고 싶니?”
256|
257|“……!”
258|
259|“개소리하지 말고 계속 거기 누워 있어. 나중에 멀미 난다고 토하지나 말고.”
260|
261|“……옙.”
262|
263|조용히 찌그러지는 혁무진의 모습에 궁기방이 킬킬거렸다.
264|
265|“멍청한 작자 같으니. 우측 네 번째가 아니라 좌측 세 번째 여인이다. 누가 봐도 훨씬 미인인데 눈깔이 삐었군.”
266|
267|“눈깔 삐꾸 만들어 줘?”
268|
269|“……미안하다.”
270|
271|“사람답게 살자. 사람답게.”
272|

Had the Demonic Cult’s invading armies not killed and destroyed indiscriminately throughout the Central Plains, and had the greatest assassin under Heaven not finally stepped forward to kill its notorious fiends, he could never have become known as the Slaughter Saint.

[P69]
“If I had not fought the Demonic Cult, the entire world would have pointed fingers at me. Just as it always had.”

[P70]
The title of Slaughter Saint was merely absolution granted by the orthodox faction once it became the master of Murim—and praise for a powerful man.

[P71]
Mungyeong had always been Mungyeong, yet people neither knew nor cared to learn the truth hidden beneath the title.

[P72]
“Why did you never tell anyone?”

[P73]
“It is all in the past. I wished to leave Murim, and I became a physician as I intended. That is how I will continue to live.”

[P74]
Mungyeong slowly rose. By then, the long procession from the Sichuan Tang Clan had already vanished into the distance.

[P75]
“Let us go down. There are patients waiting for us.”

[P76]
He had just taken his first step when his Disciple spoke.

[P77]
“A great war will break out soon.”

[P78]
Mungyeong stopped dead. Behind him, his elderly Disciple continued.

[P79]
“What happened back then will happen again. Countless people will die or be wounded. There will be no end to those who lose their parents and children, nor to the screams and death.”

[P80]
“…We will be very busy. We should prepare.”

[P81]
“You know what I am trying to say, Master.”

[P82]
“I do not wish to know.”

[P83]
“Master.”

[P84]
“I am a physician. Though circumstances forced me to break the promise I made to myself and kill again, I will not repeat that mistake.”

[P85]
Mungyeong continued slowly.

[P86]
“Fighting is their duty. Treating the sick is ours. I left Murim behind long ago.”

[P87]
“Then why have you never abandoned your martial arts?”

[P88]
“…!”

[P89]
Mungyeong fell silent.

[P90]
It was a question he himself had harbored for years. If he had wanted to leave Murim because he hated killing, then he should also have abandoned martial arts—the means by which he killed.

[P91]
Yet his martial arts had advanced even further. Proof that he had been unable to relinquish his attachment to them.

[P92]
*Why?*

[P93]
His elderly Disciple’s voice broke through his brief reverie.

[P94]
“You can treat hundreds, even thousands of patients, Master. But you are also a man capable of saving tens of thousands of lives at once.”

[P95]
“…”

[P96]
“Please prevent this war as the Divine Physician, not the Slaughter Saint. This Disciple will remain here and care for the patients.”

[P97]
Mungyeong raised his head and looked at the sky.

[P98]
Clear and blue.

[P99]
Seven days earlier, when the Sichuan Tang Clan had been stained with blood, that sky had been filled with dark clouds.

[P100]
“The sky is clear.”

[P101]
With those blunt words, Mungyeong resumed walking.

[P102]
“I should tend to the patients. Take your time coming down.”

[P103]
Dong Feng’s voice drifted after him as he descended the hill.

[P104]
“The Hour of the Dog.[^2] They said the ship would depart from Chengdu’s western harbor.”

[P105]
“Pointless. Murim is not where I belong.”

[P106]
Yet a faint smile touched the old Disciple’s lips as he watched his Master’s back recede into the distance.

[P107]
“Please… remain in good health.”

[P108]
Whoooosh.

[P109]
A wind blew from somewhere, sweeping between them.

[P110]
* * *

[P111]
“What are you looking at so intently?”

[P112]
At Hyuk Mujin’s question, I turned away from the crowd surrounding the harbor.

[P113]
“Nothing. Just checking, in case.”

[P114]
“In case of what?”

[P115]
“You little pest, why are you prying into everything? If I say it’s nothing, just accept that it’s nothing.”

[P116]
Hyuk Mujin gave me a knowing smile.

[P117]
“I already know why you’re doing it, Captain.”

[P118]
“…?”

[P119]
I froze. How the hell did he know? Even Cheongpung hadn’t heard the conversation between the Divine Physician and me.

[P120]
*Was this guy always this perceptive?*

[P121]
As I wondered, he leaned closer and whispered,

[P122]
“Weren’t you looking at the Young Lady standing fourth from the right in the front row?”

[P123]
“…”

[P124]
“She certainly is pretty. She looks like the daughter of a wealthy family too. If you permit it, Captain, I could go over as your right-hand man and discreetly arrange somewhere private for the two of you…”

[P125]
“Mujin.”

[P126]
“Yes? Ah, do you prefer meeting naturally? In that case…”

[P127]
“Do you want to sink to the bottom of the Yangtze?”

[P128]
“…!”

[P129]
“Stop spouting bullshit and keep lying there. And don’t start puking later because you’re seasick.”

[P130]
“…Yes, sir.”

[P131]
As Hyuk Mujin quietly shrank into himself, Gung Gibang snickered.

[P132]
“What an idiot. It wasn’t the fourth from the right. It was the third woman from the left. Anyone can see she’s far prettier. Are you blind?”

[P133]
“Want me to make you blind?”

[P134]
“…Sorry.”

[P135]
“Let’s try to live like decent human beings. Decent human beings.”

[P136]
Sighing, I shook my head and swept my gaze over the cloud-like crowd one last time.

[P137]
They were both definitely pretty, but the third woman from the left was more my type—

[P138]
No. That wasn’t the point.

[P139]
*Damn it. Those bastards kept talking about them, and now I can’t stop looking.*

[P140]
As I thought that, a huge man with a copper-colored complexion approached me.

[P141]
“Hey, Junior. No, not Junior. Young Hero Jin. No, Great Hero.”

[P142]
*What is this, buffering?*

[P143]
The man cycling through forms of address at lightning speed was Ship-Fire Boy Mu Song. I offered him a solution.

[P144]
“Just call me Junior.”

[P145]
“Ahem. Would that really be all right?”

[P146]
“Why wouldn’t it be? You had no trouble doing it before.”

[P147]
“Still, you have accomplished something extraordinary.”

[P148]
Fair enough. I had gone from a regional young prodigy known as the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi to a nationally famous figure.

[P149]
“And Great Hero Jeok does not seem particularly fond of me…”

[P150]
“It’s fine. He’s never liked water much to begin with.”

[P151]
Where Mu Song was glancing, Jeok Cheongang stood with his face twisted in fury.

[P152]
Beside him, Jin Wikyung was examining some bamboo slip whose purpose I couldn’t make out, while Cheongpung taught Mimi a new trick.

[P153]
“Mimi, ride the waves!”

[P154]
Sssrik, shaaaash!

[P155]
*Was she a water snake now?*

[P156]
Distracted for a moment by the rare spectacle, Mu Song finally spoke with an awkward expression.

[P157]
“Anyway, everything is ready. When should we depart?”

[P158]
“What time is it?”

[P159]
“The Hour of the Dog you mentioned has already passed. It would be best to leave before it grows any darker.”

[P160]
“…Hmm.”

[P161]
“Are we waiting for someone else?”

[P162]
I considered Mu Song’s question for a moment, then shook my head.

[P163]
“No. No one.”

[P164]
“Then we can depart.”

[P165]
“Let’s do that.”

[P166]
“Understood.”

[P167]
Mu Song raised one hand high, and the river pirates, already fully prepared, moved in perfect unison.

[P168]
Just as the people gathered to see us off began waving—

[P169]
“Wait! Wait just a moment!”

[P170]
“Stop! Stop!”

[P171]
The bow of the swift ship shuddered as it began pulling away from the harbor.

[P172]
Far in the distance, I spotted a boy forcing his way through the crowd and let out a quiet laugh.

[P173]
“Let’s take one more person aboard before we go.”

[P174]
[^1]: Hongwu was the reign name of Zhu Yuanzhang, the founding emperor of China’s Ming dynasty.

[P175]
[^2]: The traditional Hour of the Dog lasted roughly from 7 to 9 p.m.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

Had the Demonic Cult’s invading armies not killed and destroyed indiscriminately throughout the Central Plains, and had the greatest assassin under Heaven not finally stepped forward to kill its notorious fiends, he could never have become known as the Slaughter Saint.

[P69]
“If I had not fought the Demonic Cult, the entire world would have pointed fingers at me. Just as it always had.”

[P70]
The title of Slaughter Saint was merely absolution granted by the orthodox faction once it became the master of Murim—and praise for a powerful man.

[P71]
Mungyeong had always been Mungyeong, yet people neither knew nor cared to learn the truth hidden beneath the title.

[P72]
“Why did you never tell anyone?”

[P73]
“It is all in the past. I wished to leave Murim, and I became a physician as I intended. That is how I will continue to live.”

[P74]
Mungyeong slowly rose. By then, the long procession from the Sichuan Tang Clan had already vanished into the distance.

[P75]
“Let us go down. There are patients waiting for us.”

[P76]
He had just taken his first step when his Disciple spoke.

[P77]
“A great war will break out soon.”

[P78]
Mungyeong stopped dead. Behind him, his elderly Disciple continued.

[P79]
“What happened back then will happen again. Countless people will die or be wounded. There will be no end to those who lose their parents and children, nor to the screams and death.”

[P80]
“…We will be very busy. We should prepare.”

[P81]
“You know what I am trying to say, Master.”

[P82]
“I do not wish to know.”

[P83]
“Master.”

[P84]
“I am a physician. Though circumstances forced me to break the promise I made to myself and kill again, I will not repeat that mistake.”

[P85]
Mungyeong continued slowly.

[P86]
“Fighting is their duty. Treating the sick is ours. I left Murim behind long ago.”

[P87]
“Then why have you never abandoned your martial arts?”

[P88]
“…!”

[P89]
Mungyeong fell silent.

[P90]
It was a question he himself had harbored for years. If he had wanted to leave Murim because he hated killing, then he should also have abandoned martial arts—the means by which he killed.

[P91]
Yet his martial arts had advanced even further. Proof that he had been unable to relinquish his attachment to them.

[P92]
*Why?*

[P93]
His elderly Disciple’s voice broke through his brief reverie.

[P94]
“You can treat hundreds, even thousands of patients, Master. But you are also a man capable of saving tens of thousands of lives at once.”

[P95]
“…”

[P96]
“Please prevent this war as the Divine Physician, not the Slaughter Saint. This Disciple will remain here and care for the patients.”

[P97]
Mungyeong raised his head and looked at the sky.

[P98]
Clear and blue.

[P99]
Seven days earlier, when the Sichuan Tang Clan had been stained with blood, that sky had been filled with dark clouds.

[P100]
“The sky is clear.”

[P101]
With those blunt words, Mungyeong resumed walking.

[P102]
“I should tend to the patients. Take your time coming down.”

[P103]
Dong Feng’s voice drifted after him as he descended the hill.

[P104]
“The Hour of the Dog.[^2] They said the ship would depart from Chengdu’s western harbor.”

[P105]
“Pointless. Murim is not where I belong.”

[P106]
Yet a faint smile touched the old Disciple’s lips as he watched his Master’s back recede into the distance.

[P107]
“Please… remain in good health.”

[P108]
Whoooosh.

[P109]
A wind blew from somewhere, sweeping between them.

[P110]
* * *

[P111]
“What are you looking at so intently?”

[P112]
At Hyuk Mujin’s question, I turned away from the crowd surrounding the harbor.

[P113]
“Nothing. Just checking, in case.”

[P114]
“In case of what?”

[P115]
“You little pest, why are you prying into everything? If I say it’s nothing, just accept that it’s nothing.”

[P116]
Hyuk Mujin gave me a knowing smile.

[P117]
“I already know why you’re doing it, Captain.”

[P118]
“…?”

[P119]
I froze. How the hell did he know? Even Cheongpung hadn’t heard the conversation between the Divine Physician and me.

[P120]
*Was this guy always this perceptive?*

[P121]
As I wondered, he leaned closer and whispered,

[P122]
“Weren’t you looking at the Young Lady standing fourth from the right in the front row?”

[P123]
“…”

[P124]
“She certainly is pretty. She looks like the daughter of a wealthy family too. If you permit it, Captain, I could go over as your right-hand man and discreetly arrange somewhere private for the two of you…”

[P125]
“Mujin.”

[P126]
“Yes? Ah, do you prefer meeting naturally? In that case…”

[P127]
“Do you want to sink to the bottom of the Yangtze?”

[P128]
“…!”

[P129]
“Stop spouting bullshit and keep lying there. And don’t start puking later because you’re seasick.”

[P130]
“…Yes, sir.”

[P131]
As Hyuk Mujin quietly shrank into himself, Gung Gibang snickered.

[P132]
“What an idiot. It wasn’t the fourth from the right. It was the third woman from the left. Anyone can see she’s far prettier. Are you blind?”

[P133]
“Want me to make you blind?”

[P134]
“…Sorry.”

[P135]
“Let’s try to live like decent human beings. Decent human beings.”

[P136]
Sighing, I shook my head and swept my gaze over the cloud-like crowd one last time.

[P137]
They were both definitely pretty, but the third woman from the left was more my type—

[P138]
No. That wasn’t the point.

[P139]
*Damn it. Those bastards kept talking about them, and now I can’t stop looking.*

[P140]
As I thought that, a huge man with a copper-colored complexion approached me.

[P141]
“Hey, Junior. No, not Junior. Young Hero Jin. No, Great Hero.”

[P142]
*What is this, buffering?*

[P143]
The man cycling through forms of address at lightning speed was Ship-Fire Boy Mu Song. I offered him a solution.

[P144]
“Just call me Junior.”

[P145]
“Ahem. Would that really be all right?”

[P146]
“Why wouldn’t it be? You had no trouble doing it before.”

[P147]
“Still, you have accomplished something extraordinary.”

[P148]
Fair enough. I had gone from a regional young prodigy known as the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi to a nationally famous figure.

[P149]
“And Great Hero Jeok does not seem particularly fond of me…”

[P150]
“It’s fine. He’s never liked water much to begin with.”

[P151]
Where Mu Song was glancing, Jeok Cheongang stood with his face twisted in fury.

[P152]
Beside him, Jin Wikyung was examining some bamboo slip whose purpose I couldn’t make out, while Cheongpung taught Mimi a new trick.

[P153]
“Mimi, ride the waves!”

[P154]
Sssrik, shaaaash!

[P155]
*Was she a water snake now?*

[P156]
Distracted for a moment by the rare spectacle, Mu Song finally spoke with an awkward expression.

[P157]
“Anyway, everything is ready. When should we depart?”

[P158]
“What time is it?”

[P159]
“The Hour of the Dog you mentioned has already passed. It would be best to leave before it grows any darker.”

[P160]
“…Hmm.”

[P161]
“Are we waiting for someone else?”

[P162]
I considered Mu Song’s question for a moment, then shook my head.

[P163]
“No. No one.”

[P164]
“Then we can depart.”

[P165]
“Let’s do that.”

[P166]
“Understood.”

[P167]
Mu Song raised one hand high, and the river pirates, already fully prepared, moved in perfect unison.

[P168]
Just as the people gathered to see us off began waving—

[P169]
“Wait! Wait just a moment!”

[P170]
“Stop! Stop!”

[P171]
The bow of the swift ship shuddered as it began pulling away from the harbor.

[P172]
Far in the distance, I spotted a boy forcing his way through the crowd and let out a quiet laugh.

[P173]
“Let’s take one more person aboard before we go.”

[P174]
[^1]: Hongwu was the reign name of Zhu Yuanzhang, the founding emperor of China’s Ming dynasty.

[P175]
[^2]: The traditional Hour of the Dog lasted roughly from 7 to 9 p.m.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 376

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃376화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|인산인해(人山人海).
  6|
  7|그렇게밖에 표현할 수 없는 광경이었다.
  8|
  9|산서잠룡, 아니 열화신룡 진태경과 화산신룡 청풍이 떠난다는 소식을 들은 사람들이 구름처럼 모여들었기 때문이었다.
 10|
 11|비단 무림인뿐만 아니라 겁 없는 양민들까지 더해지니, 배웅에 나선 인파는 꼬리에 꼬리를 물고 늘어져 셀 수가 없었다.
 12|
 13|“잘 가시오! 열화신룡!”
 14|
 15|“사천 무림은 그대들을 잊지 않을 거요!”
 16|
 17|“뿔 달린 뱀이다! 화산신룡이 뿔 달린 뱀을 갖고 있다!”
 18|
 19|“헉, 뱀이 공중제비를 돌았다!”
 20|
 21|“화왕! 화왕이 뱀을 붙잡아서 태우려고 하고 있다!”
 22|
 23|웅성거리는 소음이 행렬을 따라 서서히 멀어져 간다.
 24|
 25|그리고 아무도 찾지 않는 언덕 위, 나무 그루터기에 앉아 모든 광경을 지켜보고 있던 소년이 문득 입을 열었다.
 26|
 27|“멀리도 왔구나.”
 28|
 29|“그러게 말입니다. 힘이 드는군요.”
 30|
 31|거친 숨소리와 함께 풀밭에 털썩 주저앉는 늙은 제자의 모습에 소년, 문경은 중얼거렸다.
 32|
 33|“……참으로 멀리도 왔어.”
 34|
 35|거리를 말하는 것이 아니다. 지금 문경은 지나온 세월을 이야기하고 있었다.
 36|
 37|“우리가 처음 만났던 때를 기억하느냐?”
 38|
 39|“어찌 잊을 수 있겠습니까.”
 40|
 41|늙은 제자는 이마에 맺힌 땀을 훔쳤다. 마치 그날의 따가운 햇볕이 자신에게 내리쬐고 있는 것처럼.
 42|
 43|“홍무(洪武) 일 년. 유난히도 무더웠던 그해 여름을.”
 44|
 45|황위를 둘러싼 내전이 끝나고 새로운 천자가 즉위한 해였다.
 46|
 47|젊고 야심만만한 황제는 연호(年號)를 바꾸고 개혁을 꾀했으나, 기나긴 내전으로 피폐해진 백성들은 천자의 뜻을 받들어 개혁에 동참하기에는 너무나 지쳐 있었다.
 48|
 49|“천하 각지에서 반란이 일어나고, 도적이 들끓었지.”
 50|
 51|“가뭄이 들고 메뚜기 떼가 평야를 휩쓸었습니다. 관군과 반란군의 시신이 도처에 가득하니 역병이 창궐했지요.”
 52|
 53|“그래, 실로 난세(亂世)였다.”
 54|
 55|죽음은 또 다른 죽음을 낳았고 이내 대륙을 집어삼켰다.
 56|
 57|동씨 성을 쓰는 젊은 목수 역시 천하에 드리워진 어두운 그림자를 피할 수는 없었다.
 58|
 59|“지금도 가끔 그때를 생각하고는 합니다.”
 60|
 61|수십 년의 세월이 바꿔 놓은 것은 강산뿐만이 아니다. 사랑하는 두 아이와 아내를 역병으로 잃어야 했던 젊은 목수는 어느덧 늙은 의원이 되어 있었다.
 62|
 63|“제가 조금만 빨랐더라면, 더 빨리 스승님을 찾았다면 가족들을 살릴 수 있지 않았을까 하는 생각 말입니다.”
 64|
 65|“후회하느냐?”
 66|
 67|“예.”
 68|
 69|하늘과 가까운 언덕에 앉아, 떠다니는 조각구름을 바라보는 늙은 의원의 눈동자는 어느새 젊은 목수의 그것으로 돌아가 있었다.
 70|
 71|“이 숨이 붙어 있는 한 평생토록.”
 72|
 73|고작 하루 차이였다.
 74|
 75|목수가 역병에 걸린 몸을 이끌고 화전민촌에 머무르던 이름 모를 노의원을 데려왔을 때는 모든 것이 늦은 후였다.
 76|
 77|그는 꼬박 하루를 울었고 가족들을 묻기 위한 구덩이를 팠다. 그리고 자신이 데려온 의원에게 한 가지 부탁을 했다.
 78|
 79|“함께 묻어 주십시오. 제가 그리 청했지요.”
 80|
 81|문경이 무뚝뚝한 목소리로 말을 받았다.
 82|
 83|“그래서 나는 네 뺨을 때려 주었지.”
 84|
 85|“많이 아팠습니다. 죽고 싶을 정도로.”
 86|
 87|아팠다. 목숨을 좌지우지하는 고통보다는 사랑하는 아내와 아이들을 더 이상 볼 수 없다는 사실 때문에.
 88|
 89|“그런 저를 스승님께서 일으켜 세워 주셨습니다.”
 90|
 91|문경은 고개를 저었다.
 92|
 93|“손을 내밀었을 뿐이다. 그 손을 붙잡고 일어난 것은 네 의지였어.”
 94|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Output contract

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

{
"chapter": 1,
"decisions": [
{
"hunk_id": "H001",

Include exactly one decision for every numbered hunk, in hunk order. `replacement` is required only for `REPAIR`.

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
